title: AT&T cuts jobs as it retires copper and automates telecom
teaser: AT&T is shrinking its workforce while replacing parts of its legacy telecom infrastructure with automation and cloud software. The company cut about 2 100 jobs in the first half of 2026, after eliminating 8 000 positions last year, and plans to retire most of its copper network by the end of this year. The shift matters beyond one carrier: AT&T is a 150-year-old company whose networks carry about 15% of global internet traffic, and its restructuring shows how AI, fiber and satellite competition are changing the economics of telecom.
